violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.waitlist_entries has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.waitlist_entries FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.early_access_codes has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.early_access_codes FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: Policy expression does not reference any column of the table
violations.message: Policy 'join the waitlist' on public.waitlist_entries does not reference any column of the table. The predicate is purely session-state — every row is admitted or denied based on configuration alone. Add a row-level condition (e.g. tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')).

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.waitlist_entries is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.early_access_codes is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: RLS-enabled table has no write-side policy
violations.message: Table public.early_access_codes has RLS enabled and 1 policy, but every policy is FOR SELECT — no policy covers INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE. With RLS enforced and no write-side policy, writes by non-owner roles are denied: INSERT raises a row-violates-policy error, while UPDATE and DELETE silently affect zero rows. If the table is meant to be read-only for these roles (writes done by a table-owning or BYPASSRLS role), allowlist it as 'public.early_access_codes' in [lint.rules.SEC022]. Otherwise add a policy covering the write commands — a FOR ALL policy, or a FOR INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE policy.

violations.title: Write-side policy WITH CHECK is constant true (open write)
violations.message: Policy 'join the waitlist' on public.waitlist_entries covers INSERT with WITH CHECK (true), so it accepts every write the command allows — this policy constrains nothing about the row written, so unless another policy closes the write side a caller it applies to can stamp any tenant id, owner, or value. The TO clause limits who may write, not what. Replace WITH CHECK (true) with a predicate that validates the written row (e.g. the tenant/ownership key), or allowlist the policy in [lint.rules.SEC028] if an open write side is intentional (an append-only audit or event table).

violations.title: Permissive write policy grants access to the anonymous role
violations.message: Permissive INSERT policy 'join the waitlist' on public.waitlist_entries lets the unauthenticated 'anon' role insert rows, gated by this policy's clause AND by the table grant. Restrict it TO authenticated (or a privileged role) and revoke anon's write grant on the table.

violations.title: Auth function called per-row in policy USING/WITH CHECK
violations.message: Policy 'see own codes' on public.early_access_codes calls an auth function in USING without wrapping it in a subquery. Postgres re-evaluates the call per row. Wrap as e.g. (SELECT auth.uid()) so the planner caches the result for the whole statement.
